response: Yes, increased neutrophil migratory activity after major trauma is considered a factor in the etiology of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). After a major traumatic event, the body's inflammatory response is triggered, leading to the activation and migration of neutrophils to the site of injury. These neutrophils can release various mediators and enzymes that cause damage to the lung tissue, leading to increased permeability and the characteristic inflammation and edema seen in ARDS. The enhanced migratory activity of neutrophils can exacerbate this process, contributing to the development of ARDS in trauma patients.
